Burlison Leads Roundtable on Strategic Competition with China | Representative Burlison Skip to main content Burlison Leads Roundtable on Strategic Competition with China July 14, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON—Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs Chairman Eric Burlison (R-Mo.) delivered opening remarks at today’s roundtable titled “Winning the Economic Competition with China: Working Families, the AI Race, and Energy.” In his remarks, Subcommittee Chairman Burlison highlighted China’s push to control key global industries like critical minerals processing, shipbuilding, AI development, pharmaceutical supplies, and other manufacturing in order to seize economic dominance over the rest of the world and undermine American leadership. He also noted that the Working Families Tax Cut Act stopped China from benefiting from American tax provisions and can be a key tool in maintaining the U.S.’s leadership on the world stage. I want to welcome everyone to this roundtable hosted by the Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs. Today, we will be discussing the United States’ strategic economic competition with China, and how H.R. 1, the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, reverses misguided policies championed by Democrats and strengthens our position to win. Just over two weeks ago, our great nation celebrated 250 years since our Founding Fathers declared independence from Great Britain. At the time, that mighty empire sought to grow its economic might at the expense of our peoples’ rights and liberty. 250 years later, the United States is the most powerful nation the world has ever known. Throughout our history, we have faced significant threats from nations who opposed our liberty and threatened our economic prosperity. Burlison Announces Hearing on State and Local Natural Gas Bans | Representative Burlison Skip to main content Burlison Announces Hearing on State and Local Natural Gas Bans September 1, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON —Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs Chairman Eric Burlison (R-Mo.) today announced a hearing titled “No Flame, More Pain: How State and Local Bans on Natural Gas Increase Costs.”  During the hearing, members will highlight the advantage the United States holds over the rest of the world due to our abundance of natural gas, how the Biden Administration and Congressional Democrats pursued policies to ban natural gas appliances and force electrification, and examine how blue cities and states have enacted laws which aim to eliminate the use of natural gas and other fossil fuels. Members will examine how those bans make life less affordable for households, small businesses and communities, including by causing utility prices to skyrocket and straining U.S. electric grids. “Natural gas is an efficient, cost-effective fuel source for homeowners and businesses all across America. The bans imposed by state and local governments increase energy costs while limiting cheaper options, making household and utility costs much more expensive. These bans also have broader ramifications beyond just those states. Democratic politicians who push for natural gas bans while claiming outrage over the increased cost of daily life have shown that they put the interests of climate zealots above Americans who rely on affordable energy to maintain their livelihoods. I look forward to hearing from witnesses on the efficacy of natural gas in powering our homes and lowering our energy bills, and what Congress can do to make everyday life cheaper for Americans,” said Subcommittee Chairman Burlison . Burlison Unveils Trillion-Dollar Pay-For in Great American Healthcare Act | Representative Burlison Skip to main content Burlison Unveils Trillion-Dollar Pay-For in Great American Healthcare Act August 12, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Eric Burlison (MO-07) today unveiled the pay-for included in his Great American Healthcare Act: a provision targeting a Federal Reserve payment stream that outside research projects will exceed $1 trillion over the next decade. The Foundation for Government Accountability produced the projection, which was subsequently incorporated into the Heritage Foundation’s 2026 American Opportunity Agenda. The legislation would repeal the Federal Reserve’s broad authority to pay interest on reserve balances while preserving a narrower earnings mechanism for supplemental reserves. The projected savings would offset reforms designed to put patients back in control of their healthcare dollars.   “Every healthcare proposal eventually runs into the same question: How do you pay for it?” Burlison said. “My bill answers that question. By reforming the Federal Reserve’s authority to pay interest on reserve balances, we can use the savings to help offset the cost of putting patients back in charge of their health care.”   The Great American Healthcare Act would allow every American to have a health savings account (HSA), raise the annual contribution limit to the same level as a 401(k), expand qualified HSA expenses, create new healthcare options, strengthen price transparency and improve access to prescription drugs. The bill would also allow families to transfer up to $5,000 tax-free from an HSA into a Trump Account, helping the next generation begin building long-term savings.   “Americans already spend enough on health care,” Burlison continued. “The problem is that patients rarely control the money. This bill changes that dynamic—and includes a real pay-for to make it possible.”  Read the Bill Text . Back to top button

House Adopts Burlison Amendment Establishing UAP Disclosure Framework | Representative Burlison Skip to main content House Adopts Burlison Amendment Establishing UAP Disclosure Framework July 22, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. – The House today adopted Congressman Eric Burlison's (MO-07) Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act as an amendment to the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. If enacted, the amendment would establish a statutory framework for preserving, reviewing, and publicly disclosing unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) records. It would create a permanent UAP Records Collection at the National Archives, establish an independent UAP Records Review Board, and extend disclosure requirements to covered government contractors. By bolstering in law authorities for carrying out disclosure, it would support President Trump’s Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE). "The government belongs to the American people," Burlison said. "For too long, UAP records have remained scattered across agencies and outside meaningful oversight. This amendment would create an independent review process to preserve those records, review them, and make them available to the public pursuant to law." The amendment would require federal agencies to identify, organize, preserve, and transmit covered UAP records to the National Archives under a statutory timeline. It would also establish an independent, Senate-confirmed UAP Records Review Board with subpoena authority to review records, hear testimony, and determine whether information should remain protected under standards established by law. The Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act now moves to the Senate for consideration.  Back to top button

Rep. Eric Burlison Releases Statement on President Trump's UAP NDA Directive | Representative Burlison Skip to main content Rep. Eric Burlison Releases Statement on President Trump's UAP NDA Directive July 29, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Eric Burlison (MO-07) today released the following statement regarding President Trump's directive waiving certain nondisclosure agreements for individuals with information related to unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP): In light of President Trump directing the Department of War and the intelligence community to waive prior nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) signed by individuals who have relevant information regarding unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP), if you are a current or former government employee or contractor interested in taking advantage of this directive, I am offering my office’s assistance in contacting and getting your information to any agency. Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence Aaron Lukas has stated that the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) will soon issue guidance to ensure that the intelligence community implements the president’s directive. My office has requested to see the directive to understand how this process will work and to assist in facilitating whistleblowers’ participation in a manner and at a pace that is comfortable for them.   Independent congressional oversight is a critical part of UAP disclosure, and we are uncertain whether the abrogation of NDAs will apply to testimony received by Congress before referral to the executive branch. Therefore, at this time, if you are thinking of speaking to the executive branch pursuant to this directive, I strongly recommend that, in addition to an attorney, you request that either I or another member of Congress be present with you.   Waiving UAP-related NDAs is something I have been calling for the administration to do, and I hope to understand the procedures established by the president’s directive soon and am calling on ODNI to issue its guidance publicly. In the meantime, my office will serve as a resource to begin shepherding qualified individuals through the process.

Rep. Burlison Releases Administration Memorandum on President Trump's UAP NDA Directive | Representative Burlison Skip to main content Rep. Burlison Releases Administration Memorandum on President Trump's UAP NDA Directive August 1, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Eric Burlison (MO-07) today released preliminary implementation guidance shared by the Trump administration regarding President Trump's directive concerning nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) for current and former government employees and contractors with information related to unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP). The administration authorized Congressman Burlison's office to publicly distribute the memorandum.   On Wednesday, July 21, 2026, Congressman Burlison released a statement encouraging individuals who believe the President's directive applies to them to contact his office for assistance navigating the process. Congressman Burlison thanked President Trump for directing the implementation of the UAP NDA waiver and welcomed the administration's preliminary guidance as an important step toward increasing transparency. The attached memorandum provides preliminary implementation guidance. Congressman Burlison continues to encourage anyone with questions about the directive, or who believes it may apply to them, to contact his office or another Member of Congress if they need assistance navigating the process.   Read the Memorandum:  Document memorandum_2026.pdf   (519.21 KB) Back to top button

Reps. Massie, Burlison Introduce Legislation to Defund Surveillance State Cameras | Representative Burlison Skip to main content Reps. Massie, Burlison Introduce Legislation to Defund Surveillance State Cameras September 3, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Eric Burlison (R-MO-07) today joined Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) in introducing legislation that would prohibit the use of federal funds to purchase, install, maintain, operate, or upgrade automated license plate readers (ALPRs) and biometric surveillance cameras. “Technology may change, but our constitutional rights do not,” said Congressman Eric Burlison . “The Fourth Amendment protects Americans from unreasonable searches, and advances in surveillance technology should not come at the expense of our privacy and liberty. The federal government should not use taxpayer dollars to build a surveillance state that tracks law-abiding Americans. Our rights are unalienable, and Congress has a responsibility to protect them.” “The federal government shouldn’t provide ‘security’ grants to cities and police departments that have gone beyond the pale and turned their communities into a version of 1984,” said Congressman Thomas Massie . “The Flock-Off Act withholds federal money from municipalities and police departments that deploy Flock cameras to surveil law-abiding citizens. Federal taxpayers should not be forced to fund the surveillance state.” The legislation would: Cuts off federal funding for Flock-style surveillance by prohibiting federal funds from being used to purchase, install, maintain, operate, or upgrade automated license plate readers and biometric surveillance cameras. Requires federal agencies to remove federally funded systems and requires state and local recipients to stop operating them within 180 days as a condition of continued funding under the relevant federal program. Withholds federal program funds from recipients until violations of the spending prohibitions are repaid to the United States Treasury.
